title: Heat Pump Water Heater Rebates in Abbotsford 2026: Up to $1,000
desc: Abbotsford homeowners can claim up to $1,000 from BC Hydro for a heat pump water heater replacing an electric tank. 69% own. Rules, a worked example and installers.
h1: Heat Pump Water Heater Rebates in Abbotsford
lead: Abbotsford has many owner-occupied houses and some of the coldest valley nights in our list. If your tank is electric, a heat pump replacement can earn up to $1,000.
cards_heading: What heat pump water heater rebates pay in Abbotsford
cards_intro: We re-read BC Hydro's heat pump water heater page on October 2, 2026. BC Hydro and FortisBC pay only when you replace an electric water heater. Replacing a gas tank earns nothing from them, and the CleanBC amounts below are for income-qualified households only.

cards.title: BC Hydro
cards.note: For replacing an electric primary water heater with a heat pump model on NEEA's Tier 2 or higher list.

cards.title: FortisBC
cards.note: For replacing a standard electric storage tank with a high-efficiency heat pump water heater.

cards.title: Income-qualified (CleanBC)
cards.note: Level 1 households replacing a fossil-fuel or electric water heater. Level 2 gets up to $2,800 from electric. Applies to a primary water heater only.

cards.title: More than one upgrade
cards.note: BC Hydro adds a bonus when you finish more than one eligible upgrade.

after_cards:
An Abbotsford house

Replacing an electric tank earns up to $1,000. A 1,200 square foot attic topped from R-16 to R-50 earns 0.02 x 34 x 1,200 = $816. That is $1,816 before any bonus, by our arithmetic.
sections: Who in Abbotsford can use this

The 2021 Census counted 53,235 households in Abbotsford. About 69% own, 37% live in detached houses and 29% in apartments. Of the households, 6,070 own a detached house built before 1981. Abbotsford's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was 0.1°C, and the coldest day was -18.3°C.

Look at the label on your tank or at your energy bills. If it is electric, you can apply. If it burns natural gas, propane or oil, BC Hydro and FortisBC will not pay for a heat pump tank, because both rebates are for electric tanks only. The exception is the CleanBC Energy Savings Program for lower-income households, which lists up to $3,500 for Level 1 and, from an electric tank, up to $2,800 for Level 2. Each home gets one primary water heating rebate across all programs.

BC Hydro pays only for models that sit in Tier 2 or higher on NEEA's Advanced Water Heater Specification list for heat pump water heaters. Ask the installer for the exact model number and check it against the list before you sign. Put the model on the invoice. A tank that is not on the list will not be paid, no matter how efficient it looks.

BC Hydro's page offers a bonus of up to $2,000 when you complete more than one eligible upgrade, such as insulation or windows with your water heater. The formula is not on the page, so ask when you apply. FortisBC lists a $300 second-upgrade bonus. A water heater is a quick job, so it is an easy second item to add to a larger project.

A heat pump water heater takes heat from the air around it. If your tank sits in an unheated garage that can drop well below freezing on a cold valley night, ask the installer how the model performs there and whether it has a backup element. The program does not set a temperature rule, so the answer comes from the installer and the model's own specifications.
installers_intro: These are the top-rated heat pump and HVAC companies near Abbotsford by Google reviews, weighted by number of reviews. Ask whether each one installs heat pump water heaters before you book. Nobody pays to be listed.
claim_steps: Check that the tank you are replacing is electric and is your primary water heater.
Pick a model from NEEA's Tier 2 or higher list and get it on the quote.
Have a licensed contractor install it and keep the invoice.
Apply online within six months of the invoice date.
If your income is lower, ask about the CleanBC program before paying.
faq: The program does not set a temperature rule. Ask the installer how the model works in the space you have.
What if my tank is gas?
BC Hydro and FortisBC do not pay for a gas switch.
BC Hydro lists a bonus of up to $2,000 for more than one eligible upgrade.
How long do I have to apply?
Six months from the invoice date.
One listed in Tier 2 or higher on NEEA's heat pump water heater list.
